claims: The Mars Climate Orbiter was a $327.6 million NASA probe.
The Mars Climate Orbiter was launched on December 11, 1998.
The Mars Climate Orbiter was to study the Martian climate.
The Mars Climate Orbiter failed on September 23, 1999.
The Mars Climate Orbiter entered the atmosphere too low and burned up.
The failure was caused by a navigation error—a failure to convert English units to metric—between teams.
Lockheed Martin engineered software calculated thruster force in Imperial units (pound-seconds).
NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) expected metric (Newton-seconds).
This caused an in-flight trajectory error.
Communication was lost on September 23, 1999, at 09:04:52 UTC.
The Mars Climate Orbiter's mission goal was to act as a weather orbiter.
The Mars Climate Orbiter's mission goal was to be a communications relay for the Mars Polar Lander.
The orbiter was expected to fly at 150 km above Mars.
This resulted in the orbiter's destruction.
The investigation highlighted a lack of end-to-end testing.
The investigation highlighted poor communication within the project.
